newsitem.title: UK: Former Barings executive cleared of misconduct.
newsitem.headline: Former Barings executive cleared of misconduct.

text.p: Former Barings executive Ron Baker was cleared on Tuesday of most misconduct charges brought by British markets watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) after a hearing by an independent tribunal, his lawyer said.

Baker, who received a reprimand, had been charged with failing to show "due skill, care and diligence" in the run up to the collapse of Barings in February 1995, and faced a ban from working in the City and a bill for costs.

The SFA, which can appeal the tribunal's findings, declined to comment on the case. It has already banned several former Barings employees including Peter Norris, chief executive of the failed bank, from working in the City.

Baker, an Australian, was head of financial products at Barings and claimed he was not involved in the investment bank's agency business through which rogue trader Nick Leeson racked up losses of $1.4 billion in trading on Singapore's SIMEX exchange. The tribunal upheld Baker's SFA registration and ordered him to pay less than five percent of the tribunal's costs.
After the collapse, Barings was bought by Dutch insurance and banking group Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV and now forms the investment banking arm of the group, trading as ING Barings.
Barings' chairman Peter Baring and his deputy Andrew Tuckey were not disciplined but had to give the SFA an assurance that they would not seek top management jobs in the financial world again.
